red_flags: Process varies by team (historically decentralised): confirm the exact loop with the recruiter rather than trusting any single online guide.
Database-internals depth surprises generalist candidates: a pure web-app background without data-systems depth is a real gap here.
AI-screening steps are reported by some 2026 candidates but not confirmed as standard - treat as emerging, verify with the recruiter.
thesis_text: Bottom line: Snowflake's entry door is unusually legible - GenSWE is a real, rolling, year-round early-career match program, so the game is less 'know the secret window' and more 'be matchable': strong coding plus demonstrable data-systems interest. Who gets in: no public cohort statistics exist, so no school/feeder percentages can be honestly quoted; the verifiable signals are coding strength, database/query reasoning, open-source or data-project evidence, and - in current postings - an AI-native, low-ego working style. Stated vs revealed: the company states values including embracing differences and making each other the best; postings reveal a pace screen ('we don't do slow') and a trust/confidentiality screen appropriate to a data-cloud vendor. Routes in, ranked: (1) GenSWE for new grads/early career - apply rolling, prepare data-tilted coding; (2) internship -> early-career conversion; (3) OSS/data-ecosystem contribution as a visible differentiator into specific teams; (4) experienced team postings. Gap to close for a typical CS student: one serious data-systems project (storage, query, streaming) and comfort discussing trade-offs past a first working solution. Plan: 30 days - data-systems project skeleton + coding practice with follow-up-style extensions; semester - contribute to an open data project or build one; year - apply GenSWE rolling and intern postings in parallel. Coffee chats: GenSWE alumni and engineers on data-platform teams; ask which teams take matched hires and what their technical rounds probe. Risks/alternatives: team variance in loops; adjacent data-infra companies reward the same preparation. Offer to execute: GenSWE application tracking, tailored resume, outreach list.

known_biases_of_data: Public postings describe the roles a company is currently trying to fill, not the people it actually hired; interview-prep and review sites are self-selected candidate reports; no licensed population dataset (PDL/Coresignal-class) was available for this record, so no school/employer/major shares are stated. Snowflake-specific: senior-posting salary is one team/level and must not be presented as new-grad compensation.
